docs.summary: A composite layout value built from independent components: `Px + Pct% + Grow * remainderShare + AutoFactor * contentSize`, plus a `Shrink` weight that only comes into play when the children of a container do not fit inside it. Lerping interpolates each component linearly. Arithmetic combines components so things like `Stretch(1) + Pixels(10)` ("10px floor plus a share of the leftover") or `Percentage(50) + Pixels(-8)` ("50% minus 8px") fall out naturally.
Raw pixel offset.
Percent of parent (0-100).
Stretch factor: share of leftover space, weighted against sibling stretches.
Content-size multiplier. 1 = use full content size; 0 = ignore content.

How readily this value gives up space when its siblings do not fit, weighted against theirs. Zero, the default, means it never shrinks. Nothing else about the value changes: shrink only applies where there is a shortfall to share out, in the way [`Grow`](#api~Prowl.PaperUI.LayoutEngine.UnitValue~Grow) only applies where there is a surplus.

True when this value contributes a content-size component.
True when this value resolves to a length without needing stretch competition or content measurement.

True when this value is purely a pixel length (no percent / grow / auto).
True when this value carries a percentage component (with no grow / auto).
The fixed-length floor: `Px + (Pct/100) * parentValue`. Excludes stretch and content contributions.
